evals.prompt: My agent keeps hitting max_iterations. Looking at the trace it calls search_docs with the exact same query eight times in a row, and the tool returns the same 40KB blob every time.
evals.expected_output: A debug report categorising this as a loop, attributing it to unhelpful tool output, and prescribing output shaping plus a stop condition.
expectations: The report categorises the failure as a loop
The root cause names the tool returning unhelpful or unchanging output
The fix includes shaping or truncating the tool output
The report cites the repeated identical tool calls as its evidence
A prevention step is included, such as a regression test or an alert

evals.prompt: Costs jumped from about 4 cents a run to over 2 dollars. Nothing changed in the prompt. The traces show token counts spiking right after tool calls.
evals.expected_output: A debug report categorising this as a budget failure caused by large tool outputs, with truncation and caching as fixes.
expectations: The report categorises the failure as a budget problem
The root cause identifies large tool outputs entering the context
The fix recommends truncating tool output at a specific character limit
The report recommends enforcing max_cost_usd before the LLM call
A cost-spike alert is recommended as prevention

evals.prompt: The agent confidently told a customer their order shipped Tuesday. The tool result clearly says the order is still pending. No errors anywhere in the logs.
evals.expected_output: A debug report categorising this as hallucination, tracing it to a missing grounding check, and prescribing an output guardrail.
expectations: The report categorises the failure as hallucination rather than a silent failure or provider error
The root cause identifies the absence of a grounding check against tool results
The fix adds an output guardrail that validates claims against tool output
The report notes that the absence of errors is consistent with this category rather than ruling it out
A golden-trajectory eval covering this case is recommended as prevention
